evals.prompt: Write tests for our new money module.
evals.expected_output: Adds property tests for sum preservation and round trips across 0-, 2- and 3-decimal currencies, frozen vectors, explicit rounding cases, and a mutation run.
expectations: Includes property tests with a fixed seed for allocation sum preservation and parse/format round trips
Includes frozen vectors for every public function returning an amount
Includes rounding cases where HALF_UP and HALF_EVEN differ
Covers 0- and 3-decimal currencies and negative amounts
Mentions running a mutation testing tool and reporting the kill rate

evals.prompt: Coverage is 95% on the payments module. Is that enough?
evals.expected_output: Says coverage does not measure assertion quality; proposes mutation kill rate, invariant tests, idempotency and timeout tests and date edge cases.
expectations: States that line coverage does not prove the tests catch wrong amounts
Proposes a mutation testing run and a kill-rate target
Lists missing test classes: invariants, idempotency and timeout, date edges
Asks which test would fail on a lost cent or a double charge

evals.prompt: Our payment tests are flaky because they hit the Stripe sandbox.
evals.expected_output: Replaces live sandbox calls in unit tests with recorded fixtures, keeps a scheduled contract test against the sandbox, uses a fake processor for timeouts, and injects the clock.
expectations: Unit and integration tests replay recorded fixtures instead of calling the sandbox
A scheduled contract test refreshes the recordings and fails on staleness
A fake processor can time out and fail on command for idempotency tests
The wall clock is injected rather than read
